info.title: Cockpit API
info.description:
Scaleway Cockpit allows you to monitor your applications and their infrastructure by giving you insights and context into their behavior. Cockpit also enables you to visualize your metrics, logs, and traces through a Grafana dashboard. With Cockpit, you can also push data from your Scaleway resources, if they are [integrated with Cockpit](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/cockpit/reference-content/cockpit-product-integration/).

Cockpit provides you with two Prometheus Remote Write endpoints for pushing metrics and logs. You can push metrics with any `Prometheus Remote Write` compatible agent such as [Prometheus](https://prometheus.io/docs/introduction/overview/), [Grafana](https://grafana.com/docs/agent/latest/), or [OpenTelemetry Collector](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/collector/).

You can push logs with any Loki compatible agent such as [Promtail](https://grafana.com/docs/loki/latest/clients/promtail/), [Fluentd](https://docs.fluentd.org/), [Fluent Bit](https://docs.fluentbit.io/manual/), [OpenTelemetry Collector](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/collector/), or [Logstash](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/logstash/current/introduction.html).

Refer to the [Cockpit Global API](https://www.scaleway.com/en/developers/api/cockpit/global-api/) for information on how to perform Cockpit visualization actions such as retrieving your dashboard URLs, managing Grafana users, and synchronizing your data through Grafana dashboards.

## Concepts

Refer to our [dedicated concepts page](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/cockpit/concepts/) to learn about the different concepts and terms related to Cockpit.

## Quickstart

<Message type="requirement">
 - You have a [Scaleway account](https://console.scaleway.com/)
 - You have [created an API key](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/iam/how-to/create-api-keys/) and the API key has sufficient [IAM permissions](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/iam/reference-content/permission-sets/) to perform the actions described on this page
 - You have [installed `curl`](https://curl.se/download.html)
</Message>

1. **Configure your environment variables.**

   <Message type="note">
   This is an optional step that aims to simplify your usage of the API.
   </Message>

    ```bash
    export SCW_SECRET_KEY="<API secret key>"
    export SCW_PROJECT_ID="<Scaleway Project ID>"
    ```

2. **Retrieve push URLs.**

   Retrieve your endpoints for metrics, logs, and traces from the [Data sources tab](https://console.scaleway.com/cockpit/dataSource) of the Scaleway console.
   The `metrics_url` is a domain that exposes a Prometheus-like API to manage metrics, and the `logs_url` exposes a Loki API to manage logs.

    - The Prometheus Remote Write endpoint to push your metrics is the following: `https://xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx.metrics.cockpit.fr-par.scw.cloud/api/v1/push`.
    - The Remote Write endpoint to push your logs is the following: `https://xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx.logs.cockpit.fr-par.scw.cloud/loki/api/v1/push`
    - Traces have different endpoints depending on the [push path](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/cockpit/how-to/activate-push-traces/#retrieve-traces-push-paths) you use. The traces endpoint for the OpenTelemetry agent is: `https://xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx.traces.cockpit.fr-par.scw.cloud/otlp`.

3. Create your Cockpit token to push metrics, logs, and traces.

   Find out [how to create your Cockpit token via the console](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/cockpit/how-to/create-token/) or run the following command to create it via the API.

    ```bash
    curl -X POST \
    "https://api.scaleway.com/cockpit/v1beta1/tokens" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -H "X-Auth-Token: $SCW_SECRET_KEY" \
    -d '{
      "project_id": "<Scaleway Project ID>",
      "name": "token-name",
      "scopes": {
        "query_metrics": false,
        "write_metrics": true,
        "setup_metrics_rules": false,
        "query_logs": false,
        "write_logs": true,
        "setup_logs_rules": false,
        "setup_alerts": false,
        "query_traces": false,
        "write_traces": true
      }
    }'
    ```

   <Message type="important">
   The `secret_key` of your Cockpit token is displayed only once. Make sure that you save it. Scaleway strongly recommends giving your token only the minimal permissions required.
   </Message>

4. **Configure the Grafana alloy agent.**

   Find out [how to configure the Grafana alloy agent](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/cockpit/how-to/send-metrics-with-grafana-alloy/) to push your data to Cockpit.

5. **Configure rules and alerts.**

   Upon creation, your Grafana instance is already configured by default with your logs and metrics data sources and with the alert manager data source. This means that you will be able to configure and manage advanced alerting rules for metrics and logs, configure contact points and notification policies, from Grafana.

   To do so, [access your Grafana dashboard](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/cockpit/how-to/access-grafana-and-managed-dashboards/) and follow instructions in our documentation about [how to configure alert rules for Scaleway resources](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/cockpit/how-to/configure-alerts-for-scw-resources/). Refer to the **External links** section of this page if you are not familiar with the alert manager or alert rules.

   <Message type="important">
     - Make sure that you select the `Scaleway Alerting` alert manager, as Scaleway does not support the `Grafana` alert manager.
     - Make sure that you create rules on the data source containing the data you wish to be alerted on rather than on Grafana (`datasource-managed-alerts`).
   </Message>

## Technical information

### Regional availability

Scaleway's infrastructure is spread across different [regions](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/account/reference-content/products-availability/).
Your Cockpit resources are available in all regions.

### Current supported endpoints

Cockpit supports telemetry ingestion and querying using the following open-source technologies:

- [Mimir](https://grafana.com/oss/mimir/) for metrics
- [Loki](https://grafana.com/oss/loki/) for logs
- [Tempo](https://grafana.com/oss/tempo/) for traces
- [Prometheus](https://prometheus.io/docs/alerting/latest/alertmanager/) for the alert manager

Cockpit exposes a subset of their HTTP APIs so users can push, query, and manage telemetry data from Cockpit.

Refer to the [dedicated documentation](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/cockpit/reference-content/cockpit-supported-endpoints/) to find out which API endpoints are supported by Cockpit for data source management.

### Troubleshooting

Refer to our troubleshooting documentation if [your pusher does not support HTTP headers](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/cockpit/troubleshooting/pusher-does-not-support-custom-http-headers/) or if [no data is showing up on Grafana dashboards](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/cockpit/troubleshooting/synchronize-grafana-data-sources/).

## Technical limitations

- Metrics and logs data is retained for **31 days**. After this period, data older than 31 days is deleted.
- The number of **active metrics time series** is limited to **250,000 per Cockpit** by default.
- The number of **active log streams** is limited to **5,000 per Cockpit**.
- It is not yet possible to downsample metrics.

## Going further

For more information about Cockpit, you can check out the following pages:

- [Cockpit documentation](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/cockpit/)
- [Scaleway Slack Community](https://join.slack.com/t/scaleway-community/shared_invite/zt-3ebz5f4as-9OBggVAbUgBksSvCCwqksA) join the #observability-beta and the #observability channels
- [Contact our Support team](https://console.scaleway.com/support/tickets)

### External links

If you are interested in learning more, you can check out the following pages:

- [Pushing logs using Fluentbit](https://docs.fluentbit.io/manual/pipeline/outputs/loki). Fluentbit is another commonly used agent that collects and forwards logs.
- [Pushing metrics using Prometheus's agent mode](https://prometheus.io/blog/2021/11/16/agent/). Prometheus can be used in an "agent-mode" that can scrape local targets and forward them using remote-write. This is useful for scenarios where targets are exposed in a private network (like a VPN or a single host) but need to be forwarded outside of it.
- [How to create a Mimir or Loki managed alerting rule using Grafana](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/alerting/alerting-rules/create-mimir-loki-managed-rule/).

tags.name: Data sources
tags.description:
Data sources are regional backends that allow you to store and query metrics, logs and traces.
Data sources for Scaleway metrics and logs are enabled by default if you are using Scaleway resources which are integrated into Cockpit.
You can create additional data sources to store and query metrics, logs and traces to push custom data.

tags.name: Tokens
tags.description: Tokens are secret keys that allow you to authenticate against your Cockpit’s regional data sources and Alert manager. Make sure that you create your tokens in the same regions as the data sources you want to use them for.

tags.name: Alert manager
tags.description:
The Alert manager endpoints allow you to manage Cockpit's alerting services.
Once you have enabled the Alert manager in your desired regions, you can create contact points and activate preconfigured alerts.

tags.name: Data exporter
tags.description: The data exporter endpoints allow you to manage and send your Scaleway product's metrics and logs as data exports, to external destinations.

tags.name: Products
tags.description: The products endpoints provide information about all Scaleway products that send metrics and/or logs to Cockpit.

region.description: The region in which the alert is defined.

preconfigured.description: Indicates if the alert is preconfigured or custom.

duration.description: Duration for which the alert must be active before firing. The format of this duration follows the prometheus duration format.

rule_status.description: Indicates if the alert is enabled, enabling, disabled or disabling. Preconfigured alerts can have any of these values, whereas custom alerts can only have the status "enabled".

state.description: Current state of the alert. Possible states are `inactive`, `pending`, and `firing`.

annotations.description: Annotations for the alert, used to provide additional information about the alert.

<annotationKey>.description: Annotations for the alert, used to provide additional information about the alert.

preconfigured_data.description: Contains additional data for preconfigured alerts, such as the rule ID, display name, and description. Only present if the alert is preconfigured.

data_source_id.description: ID of the data source containing the alert rule. (UUID format)

values.inactive: The alert is inactive and may transition to `pending` or `firing` if its conditions are met.
values.pending: The alert's conditions are met. They must persist for the configured duration before transitioning to the `firing` state.
values.firing: The alert's conditions, including the required duration, have been fully met.

values.enabled: The alert is enabled and may trigger based on its conditions.
values.disabled: The alert is disabled. It will never trigger, and will not be evaluated.
values.enabling: The alert has been marked for activation. It will be enabled momentarily.
values.disabling: The alert has been marked for deactivation. It will be disabled momentarily.

region.description: Regions where the Alert manager is enabled.

email.description: Email address to send alerts to.

send_resolved_notifications.description: Send an email notification when an alert is marked as resolved.

id.description: ID of the data source. (UUID format)

project_id.description: ID of the Project the data source belongs to. (UUID format)

created_at.description: Date the data source was created. (RFC 3339 format)

updated_at.description: Date the data source was last updated. (RFC 3339 format)

synchronized_with_grafana.description: Indicates whether the data source is synchronized with Grafana.

retention_days.description: Duration for which the data will be retained in the data source.

current_month_usage.description: Usage of the month in bytes. (in bytes)

values.scaleway: Data source managed by Scaleway, used to store and query metrics and logs from Scaleway resources
values.external: Data source created by the user, used to store and query metrics, logs and traces from user's custom resources
values.custom: Data source created by the user, used to store and query metrics, logs and traces from user's custom resources

values.metrics: Metrics data source type, used to store and query metrics using Grafana Mimir
values.logs: Logs data source type, used to store and query logs using Grafana Loki
values.traces: Traces data source type, used to store and query traces using Grafana Tempo

disabled_rule_ids.description:
List of IDs of the rules that were disabled.
Only newly disabled rules are listed. Rules that were already disabled are not returned in the output. (UUID format)

enabled_rule_ids.description:
List of IDs of the rules that were enabled.
Only newly enabled rules are listed. Rules that were already enabled are not returned in the output. (UUID format)

id.description: ID of the data export. (UUID format)

datasource_id.description: ID of the data source linked to the data export. (UUID format)

datadog_destination.description: Datadog destination configuration for the data export.

otlp_destination.description: OTLP destination configuration for the data export.

exported_products.description: List of Scaleway products name exported by the data export.

created_at.description: A timestamp of the creation date of the data export. (RFC 3339 format)

updated_at.description: A timestamp of the last update date of the data export. (RFC 3339 format)

region.description: The region in which the export is located.

values.unknown_status: The data export status is unknown
values.creating: The data export is being created
values.ready: The data export is active and sending data to the chosen destination
values.error: The data export encountered an error and stopped sending data

rules_count_by_datasource.description: Total count of rules grouped by data source.

total_count.description: Total count of alerts matching the request.

alerts.description: List of alerts matching the applied filters.

total_count.description: Total count of contact points associated with the default receiver.

contact_points.description: List of contact points associated with the default receiver.

has_additional_receivers.description: Indicates whether the Alert manager has other receivers than the default one.

has_additional_contact_points.description: Indicates whether there are unmanaged contact points on the default receiver.

total_count.description: Total count of data sources matching the request.

data_sources.description: Data sources matching the request within the pagination.

total_count.description: Total count of data exports matching the request.

exporters.description: Data exports matching the request within the pagination.

total_count.description: Total count of tokens matching the request.

tokens.description: Tokens matching the request within the pagination.

preconfigured_rule_id.description: ID of the preconfigured rule if the alert is preconfigured. (UUID format)

display_name.description: Human readable name of the alert.

display_description.description: Human readable description of the alert.

product_family.description: Family of the product associated with the alert.

data_source_id.description: ID of the data source. (UUID format)

rules_count.description: Total count of rules associated with this data source.

project_id.description: ID of the Project the token belongs to.

region.description: Regions where the token is located.

values.unknown_scope: The token's permission scope is unknown
values.read_only_metrics: Token has permission to read data from metrics data sources
values.write_only_metrics: Token has permission to write data in metrics data sources
values.full_access_metrics_rules: Token has permission to read and write prometheus rules in metrics data sources
values.read_only_logs: Token has permission to read data from logs data sources
values.write_only_logs: Token has permission to write data in logs data sources
values.full_access_logs_rules: Token has permission to read and write prometheus rules in logs data sources
values.full_access_alert_manager: Token has permission to read and write the Alert manager API
values.read_only_traces: Token has permission to read data from traces data sources
values.write_only_traces: Token has permission to write data in traces data sources

project_id.description: ID of the Project the data source belongs to. (UUID format)

unit.description: Unit of the data source usage.

interval.description: Interval for the data source usage. (in seconds)

quantity_over_interval.description: Data source usage for the given interval.

region.description: Region of the data source usage.

get.description:
Retrieve information about the Alert manager which is unique per Project and region. By default the Alert manager is disabled.
The output returned displays a URL to access the Alert manager, and whether the Alert manager and managed alerts are enabled.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: Project ID of the requested Alert manager.

get.description: Retrieve a list of contact points for the specified Project. The response lists all contact points and receivers created in Grafana or via the API.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: ID of the Project containing the contact points to list.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number to return, from the paginated results.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Total count of contact points to return per page.

post.description:
Contact points are email addresses associated with the default receiver, that the Alert manager sends alerts to.
The source of the alerts are data sources within the same Project and region as the Alert manager.
If you need to receive alerts for other receivers, you can create additional contact points and receivers in Grafana. Make sure that you select the Scaleway Alert manager.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

project_id.description: ID of the Project to create the contact point in.

email.description: Email address of the contact point to create.

send_resolved_notifications.description: Send an email notification when an alert is marked as resolved.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

project_id.description: ID of the Project containing the contact point to update.

email.description: Email address of the contact point to update.

send_resolved_notifications.description: Enable or disable notifications when alert is resolved.

post.description: Delete a contact point associated with the default receiver.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

project_id.description: ID of the Project containing the contact point to delete.

email.description: Email address of the contact point to delete.

post.description: Disabling the Alert manager deletes the contact points you have created and disables managed alerts in the specified Project and region.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

project_id.description: ID of the Project to disable the Alert manager in.

post.description: Disable alert rules from the list of available preconfigured rules.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

rule_ids.description: List of IDs of the rules to enable. If empty, disables all preconfigured rules. (UUID format)

post.description: Enabling the Alert manager allows you to enable managed alerts and create contact points in the specified Project and region, to be notified when your Scaleway resources may require your attention.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

project_id.description: ID of the Project to enable the Alert manager in.

post.description: Enable alert rules from the list of available preconfigured rules.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

rule_ids.description: List of IDs of the rules to enable. If empty, enables all preconfigured rules. (UUID format)

post.description: Disable the sending of managed alerts for the specified Project.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

post.description: Enable the sending of managed alerts for the specified Project. Managed alerts are predefined alerts that apply to Scaleway resources integrated with Cockpit by default.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

post.description: Send a test alert to the Alert manager to make sure your contact points get notified.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

get.description: List preconfigured and/or custom alerts for the specified Project and data source.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: Project ID to filter for, only alerts from this Project will be returned.

parameters.name: rule_status
parameters.description:
Filter alerts based on their activation status. Optional.
Returns only alerts with the given activation status. If omitted, no alert filtering is applied. Other filters may still apply.

parameters.name: is_preconfigured
parameters.description:
Filter alerts based on their types (preconfigured or custom). Optional.
True returns only preconfigured alerts. False returns only custom alerts. If omitted, no filtering is applied on alert types. Other filters may still apply.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description:
Filter alerts based on their state. Optional.
Valid values to filter on are `inactive`, `pending` and `firing`. If omitted, no filtering is applied on alert states. Other filters may still apply.

parameters.name: data_source_id
parameters.description:
Filter alerts from a specific data source. Optional.
If omitted, only alerts from the default Scaleway metrics data source will be listed.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

get.description: Retrieve the list of data sources available in the specified region. By default, the data sources returned in the list are ordered by creation date, in ascending order.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: Project ID to filter for, only data sources from this Project will be returned.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: Origin to filter for, only data sources with matching origin will be returned. If omitted, all types will be returned.

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: Types to filter for (metrics, logs, traces), only data sources with matching types will be returned. If omitted, all types will be returned.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number to return, from the paginated results.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Number of data sources to return per page.

parameters.name: order_by
parameters.description: Sort order for data sources in the response.

post.description:
You must specify the data source name and type (metrics, logs, traces) upon creation.
The name of the data source will then be used as reference to name the associated Grafana data source.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

project_id.description: ID of the Project the data source belongs to.

retention_days.description:
Duration for which the data will be retained in the data source.
Default values are 31 days for metrics, 7 days for logs and traces.

x-codeSamples.source:
http POST "https://api.scaleway.com/cockpit/v1/regions/{region}/data-sources" \
  X-Auth-Token:$SCW_SECRET_KEY \
  name="string" \
  project_id="string" \
  type="unknown_type"

get.description: Retrieve information about a given data source, specified by the data source ID. The data source's information such as its name, type, URL, origin, and retention period, is returned.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: data_source_id
parameters.description: ID of the relevant data source.

patch.description: Update a given data source attributes (name and/or retention_days).

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: data_source_id
parameters.description: ID of the data source to update.

name.description: Updated name of the data source.

retention_days.description: Duration for which the data will be retained in the data source.

delete.description: Delete a given data source. Note that this action will permanently delete this data source and any data associated with it.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: data_source_id
parameters.description: ID of the data source to delete.

get.description:
List all data exports within a given Scaleway Project, specified by its ID.
Optionally, specify a Scaleway data source ID to retrieve only data exports associated with that data source.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: Project ID to filter for. Only data exports from this Project will be returned.

parameters.name: datasource_id
parameters.description: Data source ID to filter for. Only data exports linked to this data source will be returned.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number to return from the paginated results.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Number of data exports to return per page.

parameters.name: order_by
parameters.description: Sort order for data exports in the response.

post.description:
Create an export to send your metrics/logs from a Scaleway data source to an external destination.
Current supported destination for data exports are Datadog and OTLP endpoints.
This feature is in Beta phase. During Beta phase, exporter can take up to 30 min to be effectively active.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

datasource_id.description: ID of the data source linked to the data export.

datadog_destination.description: Datadog destination configuration for the data export.

otlp_destination.description: OTLP destination configuration for the data export.

exported_products.description:
The list of products name your data export send to the destination.
To include all products in your data export, you can use an array containing "all"
You can retrieve the complete list of product names using the `ListProducts` endpoint.

x-codeSamples.source:
http POST "https://api.scaleway.com/cockpit/v1/regions/{region}/exporters" \
  X-Auth-Token:$SCW_SECRET_KEY \
  datasource_id="string" \
  exported_products:='[
    "string"
  ]' \
  name="string"

get.description: Retrieve information about a given data export, specified by its ID.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: exporter_id
parameters.description: ID of the data export to retrieve.

patch.description:
Update a data export attributes. Changes are effective immediately even during Beta phase.
Note that you can not change the data source linked to the export. If you need to do so, you will need to re-create the export.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: exporter_id
parameters.description: ID of the data export to update.

datadog_destination.description: Updated Datadog destination configuration for the data export.

otlp_destination.description: Updated OTLP destination configuration for the data export.

name.description: Updated name of the data export.

description.description: Updated description of the data export.

exported_products.description:
Updated list of Scaleway products to export.
To include all products in your data export, you can use an array containing "all"
You can retrieve the complete list of product names using the `ListProducts` endpoint.

delete.description:
Delete a given data export, specified by its ID.
Note that this action will immediately and permanently delete this data exports.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: exporter_id
parameters.description: ID of the data export to update.

get.description:
List all Scaleway products that send metrics and/or logs to Cockpit.
Note that all of those products send at least metrics, but only a subset send logs to Cockpit.
For more information, see https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/cockpit/reference-content/cockpit-product-integration/.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number to return from the paginated results.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Number of products to return per page.

parameters.name: order_by
parameters.description: Sort order for products in the response.

get.summary: Get the number of enabled rules
get.description: Get a detailed count of enabled rules in the specified Project. Includes preconfigured and custom alerting and recording rules.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: ID of the Project to retrieve the rule count for.

get.description:
Retrieve a list of all tokens in the specified region. By default, tokens returned in the list are ordered by creation date, in ascending order.
You can filter tokens by Project ID and token scopes.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: ID of the Project the tokens belong to.

parameters.name: token_scopes
parameters.description: Token scopes to filter for.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number to return, from the paginated results.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Number of tokens to return per page.

parameters.name: order_by
parameters.description: Order in which to return results.

post.description:
Give your token the relevant scopes to ensure it has the right permissions to interact with your data sources and the Alert manager. Make sure that you create your token in the same regions as the data sources you want to use it for.
Upon creation, your token's secret key display only once. Make sure that you save it.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

project_id.description: ID of the Project the token belongs to.

get.description: Retrieve information about a given token, specified by the token ID. The token's information such as its scopes, is returned.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region you want to target

parameters.name: token_id
parameters.description: Token ID.

delete.description: Delete a given token, specified by the token ID. Deleting a token is irreversible and cannot be undone.
